description: Costume/variation records indexed by Character::Id_CharacterVariation. Each row joins a specific character model Blueprint to its material pattern, weapon set, sound, UI images and the in-game Item that unlocks it.

ID.simple: Variation/costume row ID (character ID plus costume/color suffix).
ID.technical: FName primary key (ImportKeyField=Id in the export), e.g. CP_010_00. Character::Id_CharacterVariation is an ordered list of these IDs; the selected VariationIndex is used across battle setup, preload, capture, item ownership and UI to resolve the row through CharacterVariationDataTables (DTM +0x400).

FileName_BP.simple: Character-primary asset name of the variation's model/actor Blueprint.
FileName_BP.technical: FName (row +0x10), e.g. CP_010_00_BP. Battle preload and phase setup turn it into Character-primary loaders (StudioCharacterLoaders) and spawn the loaded AActor class; capture loading does the same through slot CharacterLoaders. GameCharacter_GetFileNameCostumeIndex/ColorIndex parse the costume and color digits from this name, and the select list rejects a variation whose FileName_BP is None. The naming convention is a trailing '_<costume><colour>_BP' pattern.

Id_CharacterMaterial.simple: CharacterMaterialDataTable row holding this costume's material pattern set.
Id_CharacterMaterial.technical: FName joined to CharacterMaterialDataTables (DTM +0x490). UGameCharacterMaterialController::SetMaterialPattern, when called without an explicit row, resolves the owner's current variation and then this row; a None value skips the material-pattern change. See CharacterMaterialDataTable documentation.

Id_CharacterWeapon.simple: CharacterWeaponDataTable row defining which weapons this variation carries.
Id_CharacterWeapon.technical: FName (row +0x20), joined to CharacterWeaponDataTables (DTM +0x4E0). Battle asset collectors expand the weapon set into Weapon FileName_BP preload names; BattleBase, LevelSequencer and capture spawn/attach those weapons. CP_040 explicitly compares this ID to CP_040_50 for a character-specific variation branch. None skips weapon handling.

Id_CharacterSound.simple: CharacterSoundDataTable row holding this variation's voice/SE IDs.
Id_CharacterSound.technical: FName joined to CharacterSoundDataTables (DTM +0x510). ResolveDataRows resolves it into AGameCharacter::SoundRow with Overrides.SoundIdOverride; battle preload and voice-player code use it for cue sheets/voices, and GamePvESettings copies the value as the default override. Note that the same-named field on Shikigami rows is resolved separately.

Id_CharacterImage.simple: CharacterImageDataTable row with this variation's portraits and sprites.
Id_CharacterImage.technical: FName (row +0x30) joined to CharacterImageDataTables (DTM +0x480). GameCharacter_FindImageRow resolves it for character/variation-based UI image lookups; battle-talk, story preload and arcade interval setup use the same join. None means the variation has no image row and UI falls back or omits the art.

Id_CharacterUniqueImage.simple: Intended link to a CharacterUniqueImageDataTable row; no consumer found.
Id_CharacterUniqueImage.technical: FName (row +0x38) serialized in the variation row and present in the export (usually None, with CP_270 variations pointing at CP_270_00/CP_270_10). No reconstructed consumer reads this field: CharacterUniqueImageDataTable is not loaded by AGameDataTableManager's loader/tick lists, and no code references the field name beyond the row declaration. Its meaning is therefore limited to the identifier-level association; no UI or asset behavior is asserted.

Id_Item.simple: Item ID that unlocks/represents this costume in the shop/inventory.
Id_Item.technical: FName (row +0x40), e.g. ITM_COSTUME_CP_010_00. GameItem_IsVariationAvailable checks None = free, else unlocked + in-stock; item/icon widgets find the variation whose Id_Item matches an Item row; select and visual-lobby costume lists derive costume/color indices from FileName_BP after checking the item. Distinct from Character::Id_Item, which gates the base character.

ImageFileName.simple: Costume image texture name shown for the corresponding Item.
ImageFileName.technical: FName (row +0x48), e.g. T_UI_Item_Costume_CP_010_00. For Costume-type Item rows, GameItem_GetImageFileName/GameItem_GetThumbnailFileName iterate variation rows matching Id_Item and return this (or ThumbnailImageFileName) as the item art; item icon code picks between them based on bShowThumbnail. No per-locale suffix is added here.

ThumbnailImageFileName.simple: Small/thumbnail version of the costume image texture name.
ThumbnailImageFileName.technical: FName (row +0x50), e.g. T_UI_ItemThumbnail_Costume_CP_010_00. Returned by GameItem_GetThumbnailFileName for Costume items whose Id_Item matches, and used by item icon widgets when bShowThumbnail is true.

FreeBattleImageFileName.simple: Character-selection image used for this variation in Free Battle.
FreeBattleImageFileName.technical: FName (row +0x58), e.g. T_UI_FreeBattleImage_CP_010_00. GameFreeBattleCharacterIndexContentWidget resolves the character's selected variation and requests this texture as a widget texture loader for the team character panel; the access is unguarded in retail reconstruction.

notes: Export contains 437 rows; row IDs follow the character's variation list on Character rows, with costume/color digit suffixes encoded in FileName_BP.
CharacterVariation is the join point between a character's ordered variation index and concrete assets/items: model BP, material pattern, weapons, sound, images and item ownership.

Id_CharacterUniqueImage is the only field without an identifiable consumer; its paired table is also absent from the manager's load list. This is documented as an observed serialized link, not a guessed feature.
Single table asset 'CharacterVariationDataTable' loaded into DTM +0x400; no numbered shards or localization variants in the export.

Reconstructed source with cited retail RVAs; some indexed accesses (e.g. Character::Id_CharacterVariation[VariationIndex]) are unchecked in retail. No claim about Blueprint-only consumers or byte-identical matching.

usages.detail: ResolveDataRows resolves the selected variation row by index.
FindVariation plus the collectors turn the variation into model/weapon/sound/image asset lists.
Material pattern selection resolves Id_CharacterMaterial from the current variation.
Variation availability and item-image helpers use Id_Item, ImageFileName and ThumbnailImageFileName.
Capture loading creates a Character-primary loader from FileName_BP.
